seoTitle: How to Export TradingView Chart Data (Download Guide)
metaDescription: Learn how to export OHLC and volume data from TradingView charts, which timeframes are supported, and common export limitations to plan around.
intro: Downloading historical price data from TradingView is useful for backtesting, Excel analysis, or deeper research than the charting tools alone allow. This guide covers how to export OHLC and volume data, which timeframes support export, and the limitations you should know about.

steps.heading: Open the Export Data option
steps.body: From an active chart, locate TradingView's Export Data option in the chart menu to begin the download process.

steps.heading: Choose the data range and timeframe
steps.body: Select the timeframe and historical range you need, since export availability can vary by plan and by symbol.

steps.heading: Export OHLC and volume data
steps.body: Download the open, high, low, close, and volume figures as a file you can open in Excel or another analysis tool.

steps.heading: Understand plan-based limitations
steps.body: Free and lower-tier plans typically limit how far back or how granular the exported data can be, so check what's included before relying on it for deep backtesting.

steps.heading: Work around common export issues
steps.body: If an export fails or looks incomplete, try a shorter date range or a less granular timeframe, since very large exports can hit plan limits.

faq.question: Is TradingView data export free?
faq.answer: Basic exports are available on the free plan with some limitations; higher-tier plans typically unlock longer history and more granular data.

faq.question: What format does TradingView export data in?
faq.answer: TradingView typically exports chart data as a CSV file you can open directly in Excel or Google Sheets.

faq.question: Can I export data from the Screener too?
faq.answer: Yes, TradingView's screener also supports exporting filtered data, separate from chart-based OHLC exports.

faq.question: Why is my exported data missing older history?
faq.answer: This usually comes down to plan-based limits on how far back historical data can be exported for a given symbol.
